text:
Jack Hughes came into this season as the man who scored the overtime winner for Olympic gold against Canada, and he has played like it. He has 27 points in 22 games, the Devils take nearly 60% of the shot attempts at 5v5 with him on the ice, and he ranks 12th of 547 skaters in wins added by his goals.

If anything he has been shortchanged. He has 10 goals on 12.0 expected (the quality of his chances), and goals tend to follow chances like that. His 1.58 expected goals per 60 is well above last season's 1.05. That fits what Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found last season: 97th percentile in chances from the slot.

The one nagging number: last season he played 61 games, and staying healthy has been the question of his career. New Jersey Hockey Now's headline put it as "Devils' Jack Hughes Is Driving Play. One Number Is Off," and the number we'd point to is that finishing gap. Our projection range for his season centers on 100 points.
headline: Jack Hughes is getting the looks
